headline: Messi called up for Argentina farewell on October 6 after international retirement
summary: Lionel Messi, 39, will make his 208th and final appearance for Argentina against Benin in Buenos Aires, celebrating a career that includes a World Cup and two Copa America titles.
details: Lionel Messi has been named in Argentina's squad for a friendly against Benin on October 6. This match will serve as his farewell appearance after he announced his international retirement last month.

The 39-year-old superstar had declared his retirement from Argentina duty in August, concluding a two-decade international career. His achievements include winning the 2022 World Cup and Copa America titles in 2021 and 2024.

Argentine FA president Claudio Tapia stated the decision was made to invite "the best player in the world, the symbol of our national team, our captain" for a deserving farewell. The event is scheduled to take place in Argentina.

The match against Benin will be held at River Plate's Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, which has a capacity of 85,000 spectators. Tapia also extended an invitation to all of Argentina's 2022 World Cup winners to join Messi for what is anticipated to be an "unforgettable" occasion.

Messi is expected to make his 208th and final appearance for the national team, where he holds the record as Argentina's all-time top scorer with 125 goals. He had previously expressed "serious doubts" about continuing to play football for "much longer" following his father's death.

headline_marked: [[Al-Nassr thrashed 4-0 by Al-Ain]] in Asian Champions League Elite opener; Ronaldo ineffective
headline: Al-Nassr thrashed 4-0 by Al-Ain in Asian Champions League Elite opener; Ronaldo ineffective
summary: Saudi Pro League champions Al-Nassr, featuring Cristiano Ronaldo, began their Asian Champions League Elite challenge with a significant defeat, raising questions about their performance.
details: Saudi Pro League champions Al-Nassr suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat against Al-Ain in the UAE, marking a dismal start to their Asian Champions League Elite campaign. Cristiano Ronaldo had a day to forget, managing only one shot on target and three touches inside the opposition's box.
Houssine Rahimi was instrumental for Al-Ain, scoring twice to put the former champions in a commanding position. His elder brother Soufiane added the third goal, further extending their lead.

Giorgos Giakoumakis sealed the emphatic victory for Al-Ain with their fourth goal in the 85th minute. Giakoumakis praised his team's maturity and effective goal-scoring, highlighting their strong performance.

Al-Ain's first goal came in the 25th minute when Houssine Rahimi capitalized on Saad Al-Nasser's under-hit back-pass. He then doubled the lead in the 63rd minute with a close-range finish from eight yards.

Soufiane Rahimi added the third goal with a perfectly timed run onto Alejandro Romero's through ball, driving his first-time shot into the bottom corner. Giakoumakis then converted the fourth after Soufiane Rahimi turned provider, rolling the ball into the Greek forward's path.

Meanwhile, Al-Hilal secured a 2-1 win against Qatar's Al-Gharafa in their league phase opener. Goals from Ruben Neves and Sergej Milinkovic-Savic ensured their victory despite both teams being reduced to 10 men.
